name: Fethiye · Ölüdeniz
tagline: Blue lagoon, paragliders and Lycian tombs
summary: A harbour town on the Turquoise Coast with the Ölüdeniz lagoon 20 minutes away. Mix beach and boat days with the ghost village of Kayaköy and the Saklıkent gorge.
seasonNote: July and August are hot and crowded; from November to April boats and many hotels stop.
arrival: Dalaman airport is 50 km away; the Havaş bus takes about an hour.
gettingAround: Dolmuş minibuses run constantly from Fethiye to Ölüdeniz, Kayaköy, Çalış and Saklıkent.
cashTip: Carry lira for dolmuş fares, beach entry and boat trips.
foodTip: Buy fish at the market and have it grilled next door; try gözleme in the villages.
buyTip: The Tuesday market in Fethiye is one of the biggest on the coast.
baseArea: Fethiye town for value and transport; Ölüdeniz for the beach
via: Direct from Europe to Dalaman in summer; otherwise via Istanbul

connections.note: To Dalaman, plus an hour by bus.
Inland road; the coast road via Kaş takes longer.

items.name: Ölüdeniz Blue Lagoon
items.summary: A sheltered turquoise lagoon behind a sandspit, under pine-covered mountains.
items.expect: A small entry fee for the lagoon park; pebbles, so bring water shoes; very busy in summer.
items.tip: Go before 10 am, or come in May or October.
items.why: The most photographed beach in Turkey.
flow: Dolmuş from Fethiye, 25 minutes.
Lagoon side for calm water, Belcekız beach for the open sea.

items.name: Tandem paragliding from Babadağ
items.summary: A 30-minute tandem flight from a 1,900-metre peak down to the beach.
items.expect: A cable car or minibus to the launch; flights depend on wind.
items.tip: Book a morning slot for calmer air; the cable car alone is worth it for the view.
items.why: One of the best commercial paragliding sites in the world.
flow: Ride up Babadağ.
Run off the mountain and land on Belcekız beach.

items.name: Butterfly Valley
items.summary: A beach at the mouth of a sheer-walled canyon, reached by boat.
items.expect: Basic facilities; butterflies are seen mainly in early summer.
items.tip: Take the shuttle boat from Ölüdeniz and do not attempt the cliff path down.
items.why: The most dramatic cove on this coast.
flow: Boat from Ölüdeniz, 30 minutes.
Swim, then walk up the valley to the waterfall.

items.name: Kayaköy
items.summary: A hillside of roofless stone houses and churches, abandoned in the 1923 population exchange.
items.expect: Rough paths and little shade.
items.tip: Come late in the afternoon and climb to the chapel on the ridge.
items.why: A haunting place and a piece of history most beach visitors miss.
flow: Dolmuş from Fethiye, 20 minutes.
Lower church, up through the houses to the viewpoint.

items.name: Saklıkent Gorge
items.summary: An 18 km canyon you enter by wading an icy river between 300-metre walls.
items.expect: Cold, fast water at the start; closed in winter and spring when the river is high.
items.tip: Rent water shoes at the entrance and go early.
items.why: A cool escape on a hot day.
flow: Dolmuş from Fethiye, 50 minutes.
Boardwalk, river crossing, then walk up the canyon.

items.name: Tomb of Amyntas
items.summary: A temple-fronted Lycian tomb cut into the cliff above the town in the 4th century BC.
items.expect: About 200 steps; a 20-minute visit.
items.tip: Go at sunset for the view over the bay.
items.why: The finest Lycian rock tomb you can walk up to.
flow: Walk from the old town.
Climb the steps to the tomb.

items.name: 12 Islands boat trip
items.summary: A day boat around the islands of Fethiye Bay with swim stops and lunch on board.
items.expect: Large shared boats with music; quieter small boats cost more.
items.tip: Pick a boat by size the evening before on the harbour.
items.why: The easiest way onto the water.
flow: Leaves around 10:30 am.
Five or six swim stops, back by 6 pm.

items.name: Fethiye Fish Market
items.summary: A courtyard of fishmongers ringed by restaurants that cook what you buy.
items.expect: Lively and loud at night; a fixed cooking fee per person.
items.tip: Buy by weight, confirm the cooking fee, then choose a table.
items.why: The classic Fethiye dinner.
flow: Choose fish at the central stalls.
Hand it to a restaurant and order meze.

items.name: Mozaik Bahçe
items.summary: A garden restaurant serving dishes from Hatay in south-east Turkey.
items.expect: A quiet courtyard; popular, so tables go fast.
items.tip: Order the meze selection and a kebab to share.
items.why: The most interesting cooking in town.
flow: In a lane off the bazaar.
Hatay meze, then a clay-oven kebab.

items.name: Cin Bal
items.summary: A garden restaurant where you buy lamb by the kilo and grill it at your own table.
items.expect: Smoky, casual and busy with Turkish families at weekends.
items.tip: Combine with a late-afternoon walk through Kayaköy.
items.why: A local favourite for a long barbecue lunch.
flow: Choose meat at the butcher's counter.
Grill it yourself with salads and bread.

name: Kaş
tagline: Laid-back harbour town on the Lycian coast
summary: A small, bougainvillea-covered town with clear water and no big resorts. Swim from platforms in town, take a boat to the sunken ruins at Kekova and drive to Kaputaş and Patara beaches.
seasonNote: July and August are hot and full of Turkish holidaymakers; winter is quiet with many places closed.
arrival: Two hours by bus from Fethiye, three from Antalya; the nearest airport is Dalaman, 2.5 hours away.
gettingAround: The town is walkable. Dolmuş run to Kaputaş and Patara; Kekova is by boat tour or via Üçağız.
cashTip: Carry lira for dolmuş and beach loungers.
foodTip: Aegean meze, grilled fish and home-style lokanta cooking; ice cream on the main square.
buyTip: Small designer and jewellery shops line Uzun Çarşı street.
baseArea: The old town for restaurants; the Çukurbağ peninsula for sea-view hotels
via: Via Istanbul to Dalaman or Antalya, then by road

items.name: Kekova sunken city boat trip
items.summary: A boat or sea-kayak trip over Lycian ruins submerged by an earthquake, ending at the castle village of Simena.
items.expect: Swimming over the ruins themselves is not allowed.
items.tip: Choose a small boat from Kaş or a kayak tour from Üçağız, and climb to Simena castle.
items.why: The signature day out from Kaş.
flow: Depart Kaş harbour around 10 am.
Sunken city, swim stops, Simena for ice cream and the castle.

items.name: Kaputaş Beach
items.summary: A wedge of pale sand and bright turquoise water at the mouth of a gorge.
items.expect: 187 steps down from the road; waves can be strong; limited parking.
items.tip: Go before 10 am by dolmuş.
items.why: The most striking beach colour on the coast.
flow: Dolmuş towards Kalkan, 25 minutes.
Walk down the steps and rent a lounger.

items.name: Antiphellos Theatre
items.summary: A small Hellenistic theatre facing the sea and the Greek island of Meis.
items.expect: Free and open; no stage building, so the view is the backdrop.
items.tip: Bring a drink and watch the sunset from the top row.
items.why: The town's sunset ritual.
flow: Walk 10 minutes west of the harbour.
Sit in the upper rows at dusk.

items.name: Kaş old town and the Lion Tomb
items.summary: Lanes of wooden-balconied houses climbing to a Lycian sarcophagus at the top of Uzun Çarşı.
items.expect: Small enough to cover in an hour; busiest after dark.
items.tip: Walk it in the evening when the shops and bars are open.
items.why: The charm of Kaş is the town itself.
flow: Start at the harbour square.
Walk up Uzun Çarşı to the Lion Tomb.

items.name: Patara Beach and ruins
items.summary: An 18 km dune-backed beach behind the ruins of the Lycian capital, including a restored parliament building.
items.expect: One ticket covers ruins and beach; the beach closes at night for nesting turtles.
items.tip: See the ruins first, then swim and stay for sunset on the dunes.
items.why: Turkey's longest beach with a major ancient city attached.
flow: Dolmuş or car, 45 minutes west.
Theatre and parliament, then the beach.

items.name: Myra and the Church of St. Nicholas
items.summary: A cliff of Lycian house-tombs beside a Roman theatre, and the church of the bishop who became Santa Claus.
items.expect: Two separate sites and tickets in the farming town of Demre.
items.tip: Some Kekova tours include Myra; otherwise take the Antalya bus to Demre.
items.why: The best group of rock tombs in Lycia.
flow: Bus to Demre, 50 minutes.
Rock tombs and theatre, then the church in town.

items.name: Day trip to Meis (Kastellorizo)
items.summary: A 20-minute ferry to a tiny Greek island with a pastel harbour and a blue sea cave.
items.expect: You need your passport and any visa required for Greece.
items.tip: Hand your passport to the ferry office the day before.
items.why: Lunch in another country, in sight of Kaş.
flow: Morning ferry from Kaş harbour.
Harbour walk, blue cave boat, seafood lunch, afternoon ferry back.

items.name: Bi Lokma
items.summary: Known as Mama's Kitchen: home-style mantı, börek and stews on a terrace above the harbour.
items.expect: Popular at dinner; tables on several terrace levels.
items.tip: Order the mantı and book for sunset.
items.why: Home cooking with a harbour view.
flow: Above the harbour road.
Mantı to start, then a stew.

items.name: Smiley's Restaurant
items.summary: A long-running harbour-side restaurant with free meze and a cheerful owner.
items.expect: Tourist-friendly and busy.
items.tip: Try the fish baked in salt or the stone-oven pide.
items.why: A dependable, good-value dinner by the harbour.
flow: Beside the harbour.
Complimentary meze, then fish or pide.

items.name: Oburus Momus
items.summary: A vegan and vegetarian restaurant with a terrace facing the sea.
items.expect: A short seasonal menu; closed in winter.
items.tip: Good for lunch on the way to the theatre.
items.why: The best plant-based food on this stretch of coast.
flow: West of the harbour.
A bowl or burger and a fresh juice.

name: Izmir
tagline: Easy-going Aegean city with a great bazaar
summary: Turkey's third city is relaxed and liberal, with a seafront promenade and one of the country's best bazaars. One or two days here pair well with Ephesus, Alaçatı or Pergamon.
seasonNote: July and August are hot, when locals leave for the Çeşme peninsula; winters are mild and wet.
arrival: Adnan Menderes airport is 18 km south; the İZBAN suburban train reaches Alsancak in 30 minutes.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; use the metro, tram and the public ferries across the bay with an İzmirim card.
cashTip: Cards work nearly everywhere; carry small lira notes for the bazaar.
foodTip: Breakfast on boyoz pastry with a boiled egg; lunch on a kumru sandwich or söğüş; mussels stuffed with rice at night.
buyTip: Kemeraltı for spices, dried figs, leather and copper.
baseArea: Alsancak for restaurants and the seafront; Konak for the bazaar
via: Direct from some European cities; otherwise via Istanbul

connections.note: Regional trains from Basmane or the airport.

items.name: Kemeraltı Bazaar
items.summary: A maze of market streets, courtyards, mosques and synagogues that has traded since the 17th century.
items.expect: Easy to get lost; mostly closed on Sundays.
items.tip: Find Kızlarağası Hanı for Turkish coffee cooked in hot sand.
items.why: The living heart of the city.
flow: Enter from Konak Square.
Follow Anafartalar Street to Kızlarağası Hanı and Havra Street.

items.name: Konak Square and the Clock Tower
items.summary: The city's symbol, an ornate 1901 clock tower on the seafront square.
items.expect: A quick stop beside the ferry pier.
items.tip: Take a public ferry to Karşıyaka from here for a cheap bay cruise.
items.why: The meeting point of Izmir.
flow: Metro to Konak.
Clock tower, the tiny Yalı Mosque, then the bazaar.

items.name: Agora of Smyrna
items.summary: The Roman marketplace of ancient Smyrna, with vaulted basements and running water channels.
items.expect: A compact site that takes 45 minutes.
items.tip: Go down into the basement arcades.
items.why: A substantial Roman site in the middle of the modern city.
flow: Walk up from Kemeraltı.
Colonnade, then the vaulted basement.

items.name: Kordon promenade
items.summary: A long seafront lawn and promenade where the whole city comes to sit at sunset.
items.expect: Cafes and bars along one side; cyclists and horse carriages.
items.tip: Bring sunflower seeds and a drink, as locals do.
items.why: The best way to feel how Izmir lives.
flow: Walk north from Cumhuriyet Square.
Sit on the grass for sunset, then dinner in Alsancak.

items.name: Asansör
items.summary: A 1907 public lift tower linking two levels of the old Jewish quarter, with a terrace over the bay.
items.expect: Free to ride; a cafe at the top.
items.tip: Walk there along Dario Moreno Street.
items.why: A fine bay view and a curious piece of city history.
flow: Tram or bus to Karataş.
Ride up and have tea on the terrace.

items.name: Alaçatı
items.summary: A stone village of blue shutters, boutiques and windmills, an hour west of Izmir.
items.expect: Expensive and crowded in July and August.
items.tip: Go on a weekday in June or September and add a swim at Ilıca beach.
items.why: The prettiest town on the Aegean coast.
flow: Bus from Izmir's Üçkuyular station.
Lanes and windmills, lunch, then the beach.

items.name: Pergamon
items.summary: A Hellenistic acropolis with the steepest theatre of the ancient world, above the town of Bergama.
items.expect: Two hours each way by bus; a cable car climbs to the acropolis.
items.tip: Add the Asklepion healing sanctuary if you have a car or taxi.
items.why: A UNESCO World Heritage site that rivals Ephesus with a fraction of the visitors.
flow: Bus to Bergama.
Cable car up, theatre and Trajan's temple, then the Red Basilica.

items.name: Kemeraltı street food
items.summary: Stalls and tiny shops selling Izmir's own snacks: boyoz, kumru, söğüş and şambali cake.
items.expect: Standing counters and a few stools.
items.tip: Try one of each over a morning, finishing with coffee at Kızlarağası Hanı.
items.why: Izmir's food identity is its street food.
flow: Boyoz for breakfast.
Kumru or söğüş wrap for lunch, şambali for dessert.

items.name: Deniz Restaurant
items.summary: A classic Kordon fish restaurant known for its Aegean meze.
items.expect: White tablecloths and higher prices.
items.tip: Reserve a pavement table facing the bay.
items.why: The benchmark for an Izmir fish dinner.
flow: Reserve ahead.
Cold meze, then grilled fish.

items.name: Alsancak Dostlar Fırını
items.summary: A wood-oven bakery famous for boyoz, the flaky pastry brought by Sephardic Jews.
items.expect: A queue in the morning; mostly takeaway.
items.tip: Have it warm with a boiled egg and tea.
items.why: The best-known boyoz in the city.
flow: Arrive before 10 am.
Plain and aubergine boyoz, tea.

name: Konya
tagline: City of Rumi and the whirling dervishes
summary: The Seljuk capital and the home of the poet Rumi, whose tomb draws pilgrims from across the world. It is a conservative city with superb medieval tilework; see a dervish ceremony if you can.
seasonNote: Winters are cold and snowy; the Mevlâna festival runs from 7 to 17 December and needs booking well ahead.
arrival: High-speed trains run from Istanbul (4.5 hours) and Ankara (2 hours); the airport is 18 km out.
gettingAround: The sights lie along one avenue between Alâeddin Hill and the Mevlâna Museum; a tram runs its length.
cashTip: Cards are fine; carry lira for small eateries.
foodTip: Etli ekmek (a metre-long thin meat flatbread), fırın kebabı (oven-roasted lamb) and okra soup. Alcohol is hard to find.
buyTip: Felt dervish hats, Rumi books and Konya sweets (Mevlâna şekeri).

connections.note: Several buses a day to Nevşehir or Göreme.

items.name: Mevlâna Museum
items.summary: The former dervish lodge holding the tomb of Rumi under a fluted turquoise dome.
items.expect: A place of pilgrimage; dress modestly and expect crowds around the tomb.
items.tip: Go at opening or in the last hour, and see the dervish cells around the courtyard.
items.why: One of the most visited and most moving sites in Turkey.
flow: Tram to Mevlâna.
Tomb hall, ritual hall, then the cells and rose garden.

items.name: Whirling dervish ceremony
items.summary: The sema, a religious ceremony of music and turning performed by Mevlevi dervishes.
items.expect: Held on Saturday evenings year-round and nightly during the December festival; it is worship, so no applause.
items.tip: Check the current schedule with the tourist office and arrive 30 minutes early.
items.why: Seeing the sema in Rumi's own city is the reason many people come.
flow: Walk 15 minutes east of the museum.
An hour of music and turning.

items.name: Karatay Madrasa
items.summary: A 13th-century Seljuk school with a dome of blue and black star tiles, now a tile museum.
items.expect: Small; 30 minutes.
items.tip: Stand under the dome and look for the star pattern.
items.why: The finest Seljuk tilework anywhere.
flow: North side of Alâeddin Hill.
Dome hall, then the palace tiles.

items.name: İnce Minareli Medrese
items.summary: A Seljuk school with an extraordinary carved stone portal, now a museum of stone and wood carving.
items.expect: The portal is the highlight and can be seen from outside.
items.tip: Pair it with the Karatay Madrasa, five minutes away.
items.why: A masterpiece of medieval stone carving.
flow: West side of Alâeddin Hill.
Study the portal, then the carvings inside.

items.name: Alâeddin Mosque and hill
items.summary: The mosque of the Seljuk sultans, with a forest of reused Roman columns, in a park with tea gardens.
items.expect: Closed to visitors at prayer times.
items.tip: Have tea in the gardens afterwards.
items.why: The centre of Seljuk Konya.
flow: Tram to Alâeddin.
Mosque, then a walk around the hill.

items.name: Sille
items.summary: An old Greek village in a valley with a 4th-century church and rock-cut chapels.
items.expect: Quiet on weekdays, busy with local families at weekends.
items.tip: Take city bus 64 from near Alâeddin Hill.
items.why: A peaceful half-day out of the city.
flow: Bus, 25 minutes.
Aya Elena church, the stream and a village cafe.

items.name: Çatalhöyük
items.summary: A 9,000-year-old Neolithic town, one of the oldest settlements ever found.
items.expect: Two sheltered excavation areas and a visitor centre; no public transport to the gate.
items.tip: Hire a taxi for the half day or drive.
items.why: A UNESCO World Heritage site at the dawn of urban life.
flow: 45 minutes by car south-east.
Visitor centre, replica houses, then the two excavations.

items.name: Şifa Lokantası
items.summary: A long-established restaurant on the main avenue serving all the Konya classics.
items.expect: Fast service and no alcohol.
items.tip: Order fırın kebabı, which comes on flatbread with raw onion.
items.why: The easiest place to try the city's dishes between the sights.
flow: Between Alâeddin Hill and the museum.
Okra soup, then fırın kebabı.

items.name: Somatçı Fihi Ma Fih
items.summary: A restaurant in an old house reviving Seljuk and Mevlevi recipes from Rumi's time.
items.expect: Sweet and savoury combinations with fruit and nuts.
items.tip: Ask the staff to explain the menu.
items.why: A menu you will not find anywhere else.
flow: Two minutes from the museum.
Share several small historic dishes.

items.name: Havzan Etli Ekmek
items.summary: A big, busy hall devoted to etli ekmek baked in wood ovens.
items.expect: Family crowds and quick turnover.
items.tip: Order the bıçakarası version, with hand-chopped meat.
items.why: The locals' choice for Konya's signature flatbread.
flow: A short taxi north of the centre.
Etli ekmek with ayran, then a syrup dessert.
